# Independent HOST-010 conformance

Scope: Linux, standard-library fake I/O and the real Python byte peer only.
No Windows, COM hardware, USB, ADC, low-voltage or ignition claim is made.
This material is independent testing, not the required Critic-B acceptance.

The implementation author owns `motortester/runtime.py`; the separate test
worker owns `tests/test_runtime_conformance.py` and this fixture directory.
Neither production code nor the author tests are edited by this worker.

## Oracle and integration boundaries

Expected wire packets, CRC32 and sample bytes come from the previously authored,
production-import-free `../device_emulator/reference.py`. Its frozen draft source
is `c54bd955aaf3cb863ef3df043ea237ea62e74ad4`; its SHA-256 is
`98bb3b6b6134f285b2e6180541dfc2d86013201f4dc2bf7924219bd088b3cd7d`.
The declared synthetic sample recipe is documented in `host/docs/device-emulator.md`.
No expected bytes are generated by runtime, session, wire, WindowReceiver,
DeviceEmulator, or the recording implementation.

Scripted invalid frames are independently encoded with correct frame CRCs when
semantic invalidity is intended. The damaged-frame case intentionally flips a
CRC byte. DeviceEmulator and SerialTransport are subjects of named integration
tests, not substitutes for an independent expected-output oracle.

Two loops each run 20 complete windows with one ARM and generation 4, using
rising/2048 and falling/1 configurations. Every sample is compared to the
independent recipe. Every capture is saved to a real temporary `.mtcap` file,
reopened, and compared before the exact original object is acknowledged.
Temporary test recordings are intentionally removed after their checks; no
synthetic file is labeled as an acquired physical measurement.

All tests use unittest checks and execute setup under both ordinary Python and
`python -O`. A bounded harness observes every pump's I/O call count and size.
Partial commands are inspected as real accepted bytes. Negative cases cover
unknown/invalid writes, zero progress, all three deadline families, post-I/O
clock changes, invalid reads/frames/ADC/CRC, stale ACKs, Stop and partial DATA,
retained results, explicit reset, callback errors and abandoned capture memory.

## Reproduction

From repository root:

```
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=host python -m unittest discover -s host/tests -p test_runtime_conformance.py -v
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=host python -O -m unittest discover -s host/tests -p test_runtime_conformance.py -v
```

Reviewed base: `45ef38792b8e824e2109e7bacc1c9dc605917d06` plus the explicitly
supplied HOST-009 transport files. The implementation author announced source freeze v1 before the final runs.
The frozen runtime SHA-256 is
`902e26df36523113aa1e1e5bc9aa9ca92513945424ec65f58b16fe956686abb7`.
`run_evidence.py` checks this and the author-test/document/transport file pins,
runs independent conformance and the full suite in normal and optimized modes,
and writes pre/post source manifests, full logs and `evidence-20261012/summary.json`.
It rejects failed or skipped runs and any source change across the four runs.
The supplied transport files were independently compared byte-for-byte against
commit `ec11d01a42e0cbdc06039ddf274121a4db7202ed` before the freeze runs.

```
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python host/tests/fixtures/runtime/run_evidence.py --deps /tmp/motortester-deps
```

`--deps` selects an existing Qt dependency directory; it performs no install.
The tests themselves remain the reusable 20-window byte/file reproduction.
Only paths explicitly listed in `publication-allowlist.txt` belong to this
worker's deliverable. The allowlist does not authorize publication; publication
remains the implementation owner's separate action. See `draft-findings.md`
for the honestly recorded pre-freeze defects and test correction.
